editions.author: Ben Potter
editions.lede: October sales data and market commentary for Devonport, Belmont, Bayswater, Narrow Neck and Stanley Point.
editions.seo_title: October 2026 Devonport Peninsula Property Market | Ben Potter
editions.meta: October 2026 property market update for Devonport, Belmont, Bayswater, Narrow Neck and Stanley Point, including sales volumes, prices and Ben Potter’s local market commentary.
glance: Sales across the Peninsula in October
Sales volume against the preceding 12 months
Average sale price across the latest 12 months
editions.trend_caption: Twelve month moving average sale price across the Peninsula, January 2022 to October 2026.
commentary: The key theme for October is liquidity. October produced just 10 recorded sales across Devonport, Belmont, Bayswater, Narrow Neck and Stanley Point.

That takes the Peninsula to 162 sales for the first ten months of 2026, which is exactly the same number recorded through October 2024. Across the latest 12 months, 208 properties have sold compared with 280 in the preceding 12 month period, a reduction of 25.7%.
The average sale price across the Peninsula was approximately $1.646m, down 7.1% from approximately $1.771m previously.

With transaction numbers this low, individual higher or lower value sales can materially influence average prices, so I think the price figures need to be considered alongside the much more significant reduction in sales activity.
For a sustained improvement in market conditions, I would want to see sales volumes begin recovering consistently rather than relying solely on movements in average prices.
editions.sales_source: Individual sales from the REINZ property export for October 2026, subject to the REINZ Authorised User Agreement. Listed by sale date, most recent first.

suburbs.name: Devonport
suburbs.note: Devonport recorded 80 sales during the latest 12 months compared with 117 in the preceding period, down 31.6%. The average sale price was approximately $1.814m, down 9.2%, and detached residences averaged approximately $2.003m. More on Devonport real estate.

suburbs.name: Belmont
suburbs.note: Belmont recorded 40 sales during the latest 12 months compared with 68 previously, down 41.2%. The average sale price was approximately $1.484m, down 8.9%. Detached residences averaged approximately $1.607m, while townhouses averaged approximately $1.146m. Belmont real estate remains one of the clearest examples of the reduction in market liquidity.

suburbs.name: Bayswater
suburbs.note: Bayswater recorded 34 sales during the latest 12 months compared with 51 previously, down 33.3%. The average sale price was approximately $1.558m, up 18.6%. I think the price increase should be treated cautiously given the relatively small number of transactions and changing mix of properties sold, rather than interpreted as a blanket increase in Bayswater real estate values.

suburbs.name: Narrow Neck
suburbs.note: Narrow Neck recorded 37 sales during the latest 12 months compared with 29 previously, up 27.6%. The average sale price was approximately $1.524m, down 13.7%. This is a good example of activity and price direction not necessarily moving together.

suburbs.name: Stanley Point
suburbs.note: Stanley Point recorded 17 transactions during the latest 12 months compared with 15 previously, up 13.3%. The average sale price was approximately $1.679m, down 24.3%. Given the relatively small number of Stanley Point transactions, the mix and calibre of individual properties can materially influence the headline average.

perspective: October reinforces the theme we have been watching throughout much of 2026. The market is functioning, but turnover remains heavily constrained.
Good homes continue to sell when price, presentation and positioning align with buyer expectations.
For sellers, the current environment places greater importance on accurate pricing and creating genuine competition rather than relying on general market momentum.
For buyers, lower transaction volumes mean patience remains important. Quality opportunities exist, but the best properties can still attract competition.

editions.seo_title: Devonport Peninsula Property Market, September 2026 | Ben Potter
editions.meta: September 2026 sales data and market commentary for Devonport, Belmont, Bayswater, Narrow Neck and Stanley Point. 19 sales, average price $1,479,500, and the 12 month trend across the Peninsula.
glance: Sales across the Peninsula in September
Sales volume against the preceding 12 months
Average sale price across the latest 12 months
editions.trend_caption: Twelve month moving average sale price across the Peninsula, January 2022 to September 2026.
commentary: September remained relatively subdued for sales volumes across the Devonport Peninsula, with 19 recorded sales for the month. The broader trend continues to show fewer properties changing hands than during the previous 12 month period, with total sales volumes down 18.1%.

Pricing, however, has been considerably more resilient. The average sale price across the latest 12 months was approximately $1.721 million, broadly unchanged from the prior period, while the 12 month moving average remains around $1.755 million.

The underlying picture remains quite different from suburb to suburb. Narrow Neck has seen materially stronger sales volumes over the latest 12 months, while Belmont and Bayswater have recorded lower transaction volumes but higher average prices compared with the previous period. Devonport has remained comparatively stable on price despite reduced turnover.

From what I am seeing on the ground, buyers remain active but selective. Well presented homes with realistic pricing are still attracting competition, while properties that are harder to compare or require more work are generally taking longer for buyers to commit to.
As we move further into spring, presentation, pricing and the way a property is positioned against competing stock will continue to matter.

suburbs.name: Devonport
suburbs.note: Devonport remains the deepest market on the Peninsula by some margin, with 91 sales over the latest 12 months. Turnover is down against the prior period, but pricing has held almost exactly level, which is the clearer signal. Standalone houses in particular lifted, averaging around $2.14 million.

suburbs.name: Belmont
suburbs.note: Belmont recorded the sharpest fall in volume of any Peninsula suburb, yet the average sale price rose 6.8%. Fewer homes traded, and the ones that did skewed toward the better presented end of the market.

suburbs.name: Bayswater
suburbs.note: Bayswater produced the strongest price movement on the Peninsula, up 22.5% on the prior 12 months. Volume fell, so the lift reflects what sold as much as the market itself, with houses averaging close to $1.59 million.

suburbs.name: Narrow Neck
suburbs.note: Narrow Neck was the one suburb to grow, with sales up 40.7% on the prior period. The average price eased, which follows from a higher share of apartments and smaller homes in the mix rather than from any softening in comparable stock.

suburbs.name: Stanley Point
suburbs.note: Stanley Point is a small market where a handful of sales moves the averages, so read the 23.3% price fall with that in mind. Volume was essentially flat. The mix simply included fewer of the large freehold homes that lifted the prior period.
